description: Urgent Account Suspension Panic: Claims user account (PayPal, Bank, Netflix, Apple ID) will be permanently suspended within 24/48 hours unless immediate credential verification or login occurs at an external link.

Visual Typosquatting / Confusable Domain Spoofing: Sender domain or embedded URL subtly substitutes characters (e.g., paypa1 instead of paypal, rn for m, 0 for o) to deceive users into trusting fraudulent portals.
Double-Extension Executable Dropper: Inbound email attachment disguised as an invoice or receipt with double extension (e.g., invoice.pdf.exe, report.xlsx.vbs, statement.docx.scr) delivering malware.
Direct Credential Harvesting Prompt: Email explicitly requests user passwords, banking PINs, credit card CVV, Social Security Numbers, or OTP codes via a web form or direct reply.
Unauthorized Access Security Alert: Deceptive security warning stating unauthorized login detected from an unfamiliar location/IP, demanding user click link to secure account.
Subdomain Brand Masquerading: Phishing link places legitimate brand name inside subdomain while true registrable domain is attacker-controlled (e.g., paypal.com.verify-accounts-security.net).
Macro-Enabled Office Document Dropper: Attachment contains macro-enabled document (.docm, .xlsm) with instructions prompting victim to enable content or run macros to view hidden text.
Insecure HTTP Credential Submission: Authentication or banking login portal URL delivered over unencrypted HTTP (no SSL/TLS encryption), exposing submitted data to interception.
Email Authentication Header Failure: Sender domain SPF, DKIM, or DMARC record verification failed or evaluated as softfail/fail, indicating sender header spoofing.
Mismatched Reply-To Address Redirection: From header displays a trusted brand or executive while Reply-To header points to an attacker-controlled external mailbox.
Fake Invoice / Overdue Billing Fraud: Email claims an expensive subscription or purchase (Geek Squad, Norton, McAfee, Apple Store) has auto-renewed, prompting a call or verification link.
Package Delivery & Customs Fee Scam: Impersonating postal carriers (USPS, FedEx, DHL, UPS) claiming package delivery is held due to incomplete address or unpaid customs clearance fee.
Corporate HR / Payroll & Direct Deposit Update: Phishing email targeting employee compensation, demanding update of banking direct deposit details or W-2 tax forms via fake HR link.
DocuSign / Adobe Sign Shared Document Lure: Message claiming urgent contract, legal settlement, or NDA requires electronic signature, redirecting to fake credential harvesting login.
Microsoft 365 / SharePoint File Sharing: Phishing message notifying recipient that a colleague shared a confidential SharePoint/OneDrive file, leading to fake Microsoft login page.
Crypto Wallet & Seed Phrase Recovery Scam: Deceptive email from MetaMask, Coinbase, Binance, or Ledger demanding seed phrase verification or urgent security sync to avoid asset freeze.
Executive Impersonation / CEO Wire Fraud (BEC): Attacker impersonates C-suite executive requesting urgent confidential wire transfer or gift card purchase for a client meeting.
IT Support Mandatory Password Expiration: Email pretending to be corporate IT/Helpdesk warning that user network password expires today, prompting verification on rogue SSO portal.
High-Abuse / Disposable Suspicious TLD Abuse: Phishing campaign leveraging low-reputation or free top-level domains (.tk, .ml, .ga, .xyz, .top, .buzz) to evade reputation filters.
URL Shortener & Multi-Hop Redirect Obfuscation: Email conceals malicious target URL behind multiple redirection hops or shortening services (bit.ly, tinyurl.com, cutt.ly).
Raw IP-Literal Host URL: Hyperlink uses raw dotted-decimal IP address instead of registered domain name to bypass domain reputation lookups.
Newly Registered Domain Abuse (NRD): Attacker registers fresh domain within past 30 days specifically to conduct short-lived phishing run before domain gets blacklisted.
Display Name Spoofing: Email sender display name claims legitimate organization (e.g. 'PayPal Support') while actual sending address uses unrelated domain (e.g. random@gmail.com).
Tax Authority / Government Refund Scam: Impersonation of IRS or HMRC promising unexpected tax refund or stimulus deposit upon entering personal identity credentials.
Excessive Received Relay Hops: Header inspection reveals message traversed anomalous number of relay servers and proxies, typical of bulletproof hosting evasion.
Unauthenticated Sender with Zero SPF/DKIM/DMARC: Inbound message completely lacks email authentication mechanisms, allowing arbitrary sender forging.
Voicemail / Missed Call Audio Phishing: Notification claiming new audio voicemail or PBX recording is waiting, attaching malicious HTML file or executable disguised as audio.
Fake Order Confirmation & Charge Notice: Email thanking customer for buying high-value items (MacBook, iPhone) with instructions to call fraud hotline or click link if unauthorized.
E-Commerce Account Locked Warning: Warning from Amazon, Walmart, or eBay alleging payment method failure or violation of terms of service.
Healthcare / Insurance Benefit Enrollment Scam: Fake open enrollment notice asking recipient to review insurance policy or submit personal medical/SSN details.
Vendor Banking Details Change (Invoice Fraud): Email impersonating recognized supplier announcing change in payment bank details for upcoming accounts payable wire.
OAuth Consent Grant Phishing (Illicit Consent): Attack asking user to authorize a rogue third-party app with broad mailbox read/write permissions.
HTML Smuggling Attachment: Attachment uses obfuscated JavaScript/HTML blob inside browser to assemble malware payload locally, bypassing perimeter gateway inspection.
QR Code Phishing (Quishing): Email body contains QR code directing user to scan with mobile device to bypass desktop web filtering and enter credentials.
Telecom & Wireless Carrier Bill Dispute: Fake billing notice from AT&T, Verizon, or T-Mobile claiming billing error or suspended 5G line.
Social Media Account Verification Badge: Phishing email offering Instagram or Twitter verified badge upon submitting login credentials.
Legal Subpoena & Copyright Infringement Threat: Threatening legal takedown notice requiring recipient to download case evidence zip file.
Extortion & Blackmail Panic: Scare email claiming attacker recorded user webcam and demanding Bitcoin payment within countdown deadline.
Cloud Storage Quota Full Warning: Notification that Google Drive or OneDrive storage is 99% full and incoming emails will bounce unless storage upgrade is confirmed.
Travel & Flight Booking Cancellation: Fake flight or hotel booking cancellation notification with link to claim refund or verify travel itinerary.
